source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed brake tests in a vehicle inspection report

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
3. Indicate the test date and timestamp.
4. Record the vehicle's make, model, and VIN.
5. Note the location of the inspection and testing conditions (e.g., indoor/outdoor, dry/wet pavement).
6. Use a standardized form or checklist to document the specific brake test conducted (e.g., brake pedal effort test, parking brake test, ABS test).
7. Write down the specific component(s) of the brake system that were tested (e.g., front left brake pad wear, hydraulic pressure, brake light functionality).
8. Include a clear description of the test procedure followed, referencing any relevant regulations or safety standards.
9. Document the observed issues or failures in detail; include no-parking-brake-hold, brake pedal sink, excessive pedal travel, audible warnings, brake fluid leaks, uneven brake pad wear, and any visual defects.
10. Record the specific readings or measurements obtained during the tests, using calibrated equipment
